\makepapertitle
\begin{paperabstract}
Layout and physical board are usually designed separately. We couple a
parametric board model, a finger IK hand model (reach, press angle,
wrist posture), and the same fast layout scorer, and search both jointly
(outer CMA-ES over board parameters, inner layout search). {[}TODO:
ablation of board features; joint vs sequential optimization gain;
robustness across a hand-size range.{]}

\end{paperabstract}
\begin{paperbody}
\section{Research questions}

RQ1 Which board features give most of the benefit (column stagger,
splay, split, thumb arc, tent)? RQ2 Does joint optimization beat
optimizing layout on the best stock board, and beat sequential? RQ3 How
sensitive is the design to hand size; what does a minimax design cost?
RQ4 Does the best layout change with the board?

\section{Hypotheses}

H1 a few features account for most of the gain. H2 joint beats
sequential by a measurable margin. H3 a minimax design costs little on
the median hand.

\section{Method}

\begin{itemize}
\setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}
\item
  Cost tables rebuilt incrementally per moved key (0.64 ms on ANSI-30;
  \texttt{context/objective.md}).
\item
  Bilevel search \#54: CMA-ES (IPOP, box bounds) outside; SA/BLS inside
  with warm start.
\item
  Ablation: ortho-30 $\to$ add features singly, re-optimizing the layout
  each time.
\item
  Stock boards: ansi-30, corne-36, sweep-34, lily58, kyria, ergodox,
  dactyl-manuform.
\item
  Hand: profile \texttt{{[}hand{]}} presets/dims and
  \texttt{{[}hand.body{]}} arms; validate with the H5 suite.
\item
  Collision: SAT 2D now, GJK 3D (\#66); manufacturability (\#73) as a
  constraint.
\end{itemize}

\section{Figures}

Ablation waterfall · layout $\times$ board table · before/after board overlay ·
regret matrix over hand sizes · morphing board with hand size.

\section{Threats}

Hand-model parameters come from literature (see
\texttt{research/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md}); costs are predicted effort, not
measured comfort. Ideally pair with a build-and-test of one printed
board.

\end{paperbody}
